starting the new era of smartphones with this invention.
• January 25 – A civil war escalates in the <color=#3366CC>Gaza Strip</color> throughout June, which would result in the <color=#3366CC>Hamas</color> driving most
Fatah-loyal forces out from the Strip. In reaction, Palestinian president <color=#3366CC>Mahmoud Abbas</color> dismisses Hamas Prime
Minister <color=#3366CC>Ismail Haniyeh</color> and dissolves the Hamas-ruled parliament. Scattered conflict continues.
• January 31 – Boston faces a hoax bomb scare, as a result of <color=#3366CC>LED</color> placards of Ignignokt and Err from Aqua Teen
Hunger Force being mistaken as an <color=#3366CC>improvised explosive device</color>
• July 25 – <color=#3366CC>Pratibha Patil</color> becomes the first woman to be elected President of India.
• December 13 – 27 EU member states sign the <color=#3366CC>Treaty of Lisbon</color>, with the treaty coming into effect on December 1,
• 2007–2008 – Crisis follows the Kenyan presidential election of 2007, leading to the formation of a coalition
government, with Mwai Kibaki as president and Raila Odinga as prime minister.
• January 1 – <color=#3366CC>Cyprus</color> and <color=#3366CC>Malta</color> adopt the <color=#3366CC>euro</color> currency.
• January 14 – At 19:04:39 <color=#3366CC>UTC</color>, the uncrewed <color=#3366CC>MESSENGER</color> space probe is at its closest approach during its first
flyby of the planet <color=#3366CC>Mercury</color>.
• January 21:
• Stock markets around the world plunge amid growing fears of a U.S. <color=#3366CC>Great Recession</color>, fueled by the 2007
subprime mortgage crisis.
• Online activist group <color=#3366CC>Anonymous</color> initiates Project Chanology, after a leaked interview of <color=#3366CC>Tom Cruise</color> by the Church
of Scientology is published on <color=#3366CC>YouTube</color>, and the Church of Scientology issued a "copyright infringement" claim. In
response, Anonymous sympathizers took to the streets to <color=#3366CC>protest</color> outside the church (after February 10), while the
church's websites and centres were getting <color=#3366CC>DoS attacks</color>, phone line nukes, and black faxes.
• February 16 – Kosovo unilaterally declares independence from <color=#3366CC>Serbia</color>. Serbia refuses to recognize it and considers
Kosovo as part of its territory.
• February 18 – <color=#3366CC>WikiLeaks</color> releases allegations of <color=#3366CC>illegal activities</color> carried out by the <color=#3366CC>Cayman Islands</color> branch of
Swiss banking corporation Julius Baer; a subsequent lawsuit against WikiLeaks prompts a <color=#3366CC>temporary suspension</color>
of the website, but uproar about violations of <color=#3366CC>freedom of speech</color> causes WikiLeaks to be brought back online.
• May 2 – Cyclone Nargis kills 133,000 in <color=#3366CC>Myanmar</color>.
• May 12 – <color=#3366CC>Magnitude 8.0 earthquake</color> occurs in Wenchuan, China, causing almost 90,000 people to die or go
missing.
• May 28 – The 1st Nepalese Constituent Assembly declares <color=#3366CC>Nepal</color> a <color=#3366CC>republic</color>, ending its monarchy.
• August 1–12 – <color=#3366CC>An armed conflict</color> is fought between <color=#3366CC>Georgia</color> and the <color=#3366CC>Russian Federation</color> together with Ossetian
and Abkhazian separatists on the other. Russia officially recognizes the independence of <color=#3366CC>Abkhazia</color> and <color=#3366CC>South</color>
<color=#3366CC>Ossetia</color>.
• November 4 – <color=#3366CC>Barack Obama</color> is elected as the first African-American <color=#3366CC>president of the United States</color>. He is sworn
into office on January 20, 2009.
• November 26–29 – The financial capital of <color=#3366CC>India</color>, <color=#3366CC>Mumbai</color>, is <color=#3366CC>attacked</color> by ten Pakistani terrorists belonging to
Lashkar-e-Taiba, resulting in 175 deaths (including nine attackers). One gunman, named Ajmal Amir Kasab, is
captured alive by Mumbai Police and executed on 21 November 2012.
• December 11 – Following the release of its beta version on September 2, <color=#3366CC>Google Chrome</color> 1.0 is released.
• January 3 – The <color=#3366CC>cryptocurrency</color> <color=#3366CC>Bitcoin</color> is launched.
• January 15 – US Airways Flight 1549 ditches in the <color=#3366CC>Hudson River</color> in an accident that becomes known as the
"Miracle on the Hudson", as all 155 people on board are rescued.
• April 1 – <color=#3366CC>Albania</color> and <color=#3366CC>Croatia</color> join <color=#3366CC>NATO</color>.
• April 5 – <color=#3366CC>North Korea</color> launches a rocket from its Tonghae Satellite Launching Ground, which it says is carrying the

• April 7 – April 2009 Moldovan parliamentary election protests – In protests that spurred across Moldova, claiming a
fraudulent election had occurred, 4 people died and 270 were injured.
• April 21 – <color=#3366CC>UNESCO</color> launches the World Digital Library.
• June 13 – Protests erupt in <color=#3366CC>Iran</color>, following the presidential election, against Iranian president <color=#3366CC>Mahmoud</color>
<color=#3366CC>Ahmadinejad</color>.
• June 16 – <color=#3366CC>BRIC</color> is formed by <color=#3366CC>Brazil</color>, <color=#3366CC>Russia</color>, <color=#3366CC>India</color>, and <color=#3366CC>China</color>, as an economic bloc.
• June 25 – American pop star <color=#3366CC>Michael Jackson</color> dies at the age of 50. His death triggers an outpouring of worldwide
grief; online reactions to the event cripple several major websites and services, as the abundance of people
accessing the <color=#3366CC>web addresses</color> pushes internet traffic to unprecedented and historic levels.
• November 23 – At least 58 people are abducted and killed in the then-province of Maguindanao (now
Maguindanao del Sur, <color=#3366CC>Philippines</color>, in what the Committee to Protect Journalists called the single deadliest attack
on journalists in history.
• February 25 – Kamla Persad-Bissessar becomes the first female prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago.
• April 10 – Polish President <color=#3366CC>Lech Kaczyński</color> dies in an airplane crash near the city of Smolensk, Russia, along with
his wife and 94 other people on board.
• May 10 – <color=#3366CC>Benigno Aquino III</color> is the first bachelor President of the Philippines and the second to be the child of a
<color=#3366CC>previous president</color>.
• June 11 – July 11 – <color=#3366CC>South Africa</color> becomes the first country in <color=#3366CC>Africa</color> to host the FIFA World Cup.
• June 24 – <color=#3366CC>Julia Gillard</color> becomes the first female Prime Minister of Australia.
• October 3 – <color=#3366CC>Dilma Rousseff</color> is elected as the first female president of Brazil. She serves as the president until her

<color=#3366CC>Middle East</color> and the <color=#3366CC>Arab world</color>, with widespread <color=#3366CC>protests</color>, demonstrations, <color=#3366CC>riots</color> and <color=#3366CC>civil wars</color> for <color=#3366CC>free elections</color>
and <color=#3366CC>human rights</color>.
• March 11 – The <color=#3366CC>2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami</color> and subsequent <color=#3366CC>Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster</color> in
<color=#3366CC>Japan</color> leave 15,899 people dead.
• May 2 – <color=#3366CC>Al-Qaeda</color> leader <color=#3366CC>Osama bin Laden</color>, the mastermind behind the 9/11 attacks, is <color=#3366CC>killed in a raid</color> at his
compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan by the U.S. Navy's SEAL Team 6 (DEVGRU).
• July 10 – Britain's largest tabloid newspaper, the <color=#3366CC>News of the World</color>, shuts down after 168 years in print due to the
2009 phone hacking scandal.
• July 14 – <color=#3366CC>South Sudan</color>, following the <color=#3366CC>January 2011 independence referendum</color>, becomes a member of the <color=#3366CC>United</color>
<color=#3366CC>Nations</color>.
• September 17 – The <color=#3366CC>Occupy movement</color>, an international protest movement against <color=#3366CC>social</color> and <color=#3366CC>economic</color>
<color=#3366CC>inequality</color>, takes shape. It is partially inspired by the Arab Spring and is one of the first significant global protest
movements to occur in the age of <color=#3366CC>social media</color>.
• October 20 – Deposed dictator <color=#3366CC>Muammar Gaddafi</color> is captured and killed by the National Liberation Army of Libya,

sexual scandals.
• December 15 – The <color=#3366CC>Iraq War</color> is formally declared over.

paramount leader of <color=#3366CC>China</color> after <color=#3366CC>Hu Jintao</color>.
• December 10 – Séléka rebels seize power in the <color=#3366CC>Central African Republic</color>, ousting the president and government
and beginning a <color=#3366CC>civil war</color>.
• December 19 – <color=#3366CC>Park Geun-hye</color> is elected President of South Korea, the first woman to hold the position.
• January 11 – <color=#3366CC>France</color> intervenes with its army in the <color=#3366CC>Northern Mali conflict</color>, defeating the Islamists who had taken
control of the country.

pope emeritus. At the subsequent papal conclave, Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Argentina is elected pope on

• March 5 – President of Venezuela <color=#3366CC>Hugo Chávez</color> dies due to prostate cancer and is succeeded by <color=#3366CC>Nicolás Maduro</color>.

stroke.
• July 1 – <color=#3366CC>Croatia</color> becomes the 28th member of the <color=#3366CC>European Union</color>.
• September 14 – <color=#3366CC>Syria</color> avoids an American intervention on its soil during the <color=#3366CC>Syrian Civil War</color>, accepting to destroy
all chemical weapons stocks owned.

• <color=#3366CC>November</color> – <color=#3366CC>China</color> declares an "Air Defense Identification Zone" in the <color=#3366CC>East China Sea</color>, including over the <color=#3366CC>Senkaku</color>
<color=#3366CC>Islands</color>, a group of islands held by Japan, but claimed by both Japan and China, and the Socotra Rock, claimed by
both China and South Korea.

• December 15 – The <color=#3366CC>South Sudanese Civil War</color> breaks out.
• <color=#3366CC>Iran</color> allows international inspections on its nuclear policy in exchange of the removal of the sanctions and the right
to produce a small amount of low-grade enriched uranium, thus marking an apparent new policy towards the
<color=#3366CC>United Nations</color> under <color=#3366CC>Hassan Rohani</color>'s presidency.
• 2013–2014 – A political crisis in Thailand breaks out and the government declares <color=#3366CC>martial law</color>.
• February 22 – Pro-Russian President of Ukraine <color=#3366CC>Viktor Yanukovich</color> is ousted amidst the <color=#3366CC>Euromaidan</color> revolution.

The <color=#3366CC>Russian Federation</color> <color=#3366CC>annexes</color> <color=#3366CC>Crimea</color> in response, and a "low intensity" <color=#3366CC>war in Donbas</color> breaks out between the
Ukrainian government and Russian-backed separatists.
• May 26 – <color=#3366CC>Narendra Modi</color> becomes 14th Prime Minister of <color=#3366CC>India</color>, winning a clear majority in the election.
• September 18 – <color=#3366CC>Scotland</color> votes to remain part of the <color=#3366CC>United Kingdom</color> during the 2014 Scottish independence
referendum.

territories in northern <color=#3366CC>Iraq</color> and Syria, near the border with Turkey. The <color=#3366CC>United States</color> lead a coalition of more than
30 countries <color=#3366CC>to destroy ISIL</color>. Meanwhile, <color=#3366CC>Russia</color> leads its own coalition, along with Syria, Iraq and Iran, and
Russia's military action begins on September 30, 2015.
• October 31 – In <color=#3366CC>Burkina Faso</color>, President <color=#3366CC>Blaise Compaoré</color> resigns amidst widespread protests, ending 27 years of
leadership.

<color=#3366CC>Raúl Castro</color> announce the beginning of a process of normalizing relations between Cuba and the United States,
ending a 54-year stretch of hostility between the two nations. Later, on July 20, 2015, with full diplomatic relations,
the embassies of both countries are opened after five decades.
• January 7 – Two gunmen, brothers Saïd and Chérif Kouachi, commit <color=#3366CC>a mass murder</color> at the offices of Charlie
Hebdo in <color=#3366CC>Paris</color>, killing 12 people. Following the attack, about two million people, including more than 40 world
leaders, met in Paris for a rally of national unity, and 3.7 million people joined demonstrations across the country.
The phrase Je suis Charlie became a common slogan of support at the rallies and in social media.
• March 6 – <color=#3366CC>NASA</color>'s Dawn probe enters orbit around <color=#3366CC>Ceres</color>, becoming the first spacecraft to visit a <color=#3366CC>dwarf planet</color>.

and 4 in <color=#3366CC>Bangladesh</color> with a total of 9,018 deaths.

marry in a landmark case Obergefell v. Hodges.
• July 14 – The P5+1 (China, France, Russia, the UK, and the US + Germany) and <color=#3366CC>Iran</color> agree on final provisions of
Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action in regards to the latter's nuclear program.
• <color=#3366CC>October</color> – The <color=#3366CC>Chinese Communist Party</color> announces the end of the <color=#3366CC>one-child policy</color> after 35 years.

member destroying a Russian aircraft since the attack on the Sui-ho Dam (during the <color=#3366CC>Korean War</color>).
• November 30 – December 12 – During the UN summit on Climate Change, 193 nations <color=#3366CC>agree</color> to reduce carbon
emissions starting in 2020.
• During the <color=#3366CC>2015 European migrant crisis</color>, around 1.3 million people, most notably <color=#3366CC>refugees</color> of the wars in <color=#3366CC>Syria</color>,
Iraq and <color=#3366CC>Afghanistan</color>, flee to Europe to claim <color=#3366CC>asylum</color>, leading to considerable political upheaval in the <color=#3366CC>European</color>
<color=#3366CC>Union</color>. <color=#3366CC>Germany</color> ultimately takes in the majority of the asylum seekers.
• January 3 – Following the fallout caused by the <color=#3366CC>execution of Nimr al-Nimr</color>, <color=#3366CC>Saudi Arabia</color> and several other
countries end their diplomatic relations with <color=#3366CC>Iran</color>.
• January 8 – <color=#3366CC>Joaquín Guzmán</color>, widely regarded as the world's most powerful drug trafficker, is recaptured following
his escape from a maximum-security prison in Mexico.
• January 16
• The <color=#3366CC>International Atomic Energy Agency</color> announces that Iran has adequately dismantled its nuclear weapons
program, allowing the <color=#3366CC>United Nations</color> to lift sanctions immediately.
• In the general election of the Republic of China (Taiwan), the Democratic Progressive Party, led by <color=#3366CC>Tsai Ing-wen</color>,
secured a majority in the Legislative Yuan, resulting in the first majority by a non-KMT party and the first majority
won by the DPP. Tsai become the 14th President for <color=#3366CC>Taiwan</color>, and also become the first female leader for China.
• January 28 – The <color=#3366CC>World Health Organization</color> announces an <color=#3366CC>outbreak</color> of the Zika virus.
• May 9 – <color=#3366CC>Rodrigo Duterte</color> becomes the first <color=#3366CC>Mindanaoan</color> President of the Philippines and the oldest person ever
elected to the presidency.
• June 5 – <color=#3366CC>Hillary Clinton</color> becomes the <color=#3366CC>Democratic Party</color>'s nominee for president of the United States, making her
the first woman to be nominated for president by a major party.
• June 23 – The <color=#3366CC>United Kingdom</color> votes to <color=#3366CC>leave the European Union</color> in the June 2016 membership referendum.
• July 15–16 – A <color=#3366CC>coup d'état</color> is attempted in Turkey against state institutions, including but not limited to the
government and President <color=#3366CC>Recep Tayyip Erdoğan</color>. The attempt is carried out by a faction within the Turkish Armed
Forces that organized themselves as the Peace at Home Council.
• September 2 – 1st President of Uzbekistan <color=#3366CC>Islam Karimov</color> dies at age of 78, after 25 years in office.
• September 28 – Former President of Israel and 1994 Nobel Peace Prize laureate <color=#3366CC>Shimon Peres</color> dies at the age of

Science and technology
Space exploration
Beginning on 3 November 2000, humans have had an uninterrupted presence in space which has lasted to this day.
This is because of the <color=#3366CC>International Space Station</color>, a spacecraft that was assembled in low Earth orbit with a series of
interconnected modules, <color=#3366CC>solar panels</color>, radiators, and eight docking ports, with the first module being launched in 1998.
Until its planned retirement in 2030, it will continue to host astronauts that will pioneer in scientific research and
spacecraft control. Private spaceflight became increasingly common with non-government-funded companies making
more and more technological advancements. <color=#3366CC>SpaceX</color>, founded by <color=#3366CC>Elon Musk</color>, wishes to pave the way for a
self-sustaining colony on Mars to ensure the survival of humanity. In the early 2020s, some journalists have used the
phrase "New Space Age" in reference to a resurgence of innovation and public interest in space exploration as well as
commercial applications of <color=#3366CC>low Earth orbit</color> (LEO) and more distant destinations. New developments include the
participation of billionaires in crewed space travel, including <color=#3366CC>space tourism</color> and interplanetary travel.
There were also major achievements in the exploration of the <color=#3366CC>Solar System</color>. <color=#3366CC>Minor planets</color> were first widely explored,
including <color=#3366CC>an asteroid</color> in 2001, a comet in 2005, and <color=#3366CC>a dwarf planet</color> in 2015. In 2022, an asteroid's moon (Dimorphos,
orbiting Didymos) was impacted by the Double Asteroid Redirection Test to test a method of planetary defense. On
<color=#3366CC>Mars</color>, spacecraft Phoenix found water on the planet in 2008; 5 <color=#3366CC>new rovers</color> were also deployed on the planet, along with
the first Mars helicopter.
In the Outer Solar System, planetary orbiters received groundbreaking new data from <color=#3366CC>Jupiter</color> and <color=#3366CC>Saturn</color>. At Jupiter,
the Galileo orbiter was retired in 2003 and replaced with a second scientific orbiter in 2016. At Saturn,
<color=#3366CC>Cassini–Huygens</color> allowed numerous remarkable scientific discoveries to be found. After entry into Saturn's orbit, the
Huygens component successfully landed on the atmospheric moon <color=#3366CC>Titan</color> in 2005, the first-ever extraterrestrial moon to
be landed on – in 2007, the Cassini orbiter confirmed the existence of <color=#3366CC>liquid lakes on Titan</color>. The orbiter also discovered
the first cryovolcano (on <color=#3366CC>Enceladus</color>); studied the <color=#3366CC>rings of Saturn</color> in detail; and was retired in 2017. <color=#3366CC>Pluto</color> and its moon
<color=#3366CC>Charon</color> were visited for the first time in 2015 with <color=#3366CC>New Horizons</color>. Going even further, spacecraft <color=#3366CC>Voyager 1</color>, launched in
1977, became the first spacecraft to reach <color=#3366CC>interstellar space</color> in 2012.
In 2017, the first confirmed <color=#3366CC>visitor from another star system</color> (<color=#3366CC>1I/Oumuamua</color>) was seen passing by <color=#3366CC>Earth</color>. It is one of
three known interstellar objects known to be currently passing through the <color=#3366CC>Solar System</color>, all three of which have
unusual characteristics. In 2019, the first photograph of a <color=#3366CC>black hole</color> (<color=#3366CC>Messier 87</color>) was captured. The number of
<color=#3366CC>exoplanets</color> known dramatically increased, with 6,042 being known as of 2025, some of which are in the <color=#3366CC>habitable zone</color>
and exhibit possible biosignatures.

The <color=#3366CC>Digital Revolution</color> continued into the early 21st century with mobile phone usage and Global Internet usage
growing massively, becoming available to many more people, with more applications and faster speeds.
<color=#3366CC>Social networking</color> emerged in the mid-2000s as a popular form of social communication, partly replacing much of the

function of <color=#3366CC>email</color>, <color=#3366CC>message boards</color> and <color=#3366CC>instant messaging</color> services. <color=#3366CC>Twitter</color>, <color=#3366CC>Facebook</color>, <color=#3366CC>YouTube</color>, <color=#3366CC>Instagram</color>, <color=#3366CC>Snapchat</color>
and WeChat are all major examples of social media which have gained widespread popularity. The use of <color=#3366CC>webcams</color>

<color=#3366CC>video calling</color> and <color=#3366CC>video conferencing</color> widespread. Their use hugely increased during the <color=#3366CC>COVID-19 pandemic</color>.

massive-scale oil spill that may become one of the worst environmental disasters in <color=#3366CC>United States</color> history. On 18
June 2010, oceanographer John Kessler said that the crude gushing from the well contains 40 percent methane,
compared to about 5 percent found in typical oil deposits. Methane is a natural gas that could potentially suffocate
marine life and create "dead zones" where oxygen is so depleted that nothing lives. "This is the most vigorous
methane eruption in modern human history", Kessler said. On 20 June an internal BP document was released by
Congress revealing that BP estimated the flow could be as much as 100000 oilbbl per day under the circumstances
that existed since 20 April blowout.
Pandemics and epidemics
Several epidemics and pandemics have defined the early century. In 2013, an <color=#3366CC>epidemic of the Ebola Virus</color> began in
<color=#3366CC>West Africa</color>. After cases reached their peak in October 2014 and the epidemic was over by 2016, the infection count
had reached 28,646 cases and 11,323 deaths – an extraordinarily high case-fatality rate (40%).
There have been two epidemics and pandemics involving <color=#3366CC>severe acute respiratory syndrome</color>: the <color=#3366CC>2002–2004 outbreak</color>
with the variant SARS-CoV-1 that began in China, leading to 8,000 infections and 774 deaths worldwide; and in 2020,
the virus strain <color=#3366CC>SARS-CoV-2</color> caused <color=#3366CC>an outbreak</color> of the <color=#3366CC>coronavirus disease</color>. Its societal impacts were numerous:
lockdowns were imposed, which contributed to <color=#3366CC>economic stagnation</color>. The death toll from the pandemic could be as high
as 33 million, and it is widely considered to be in the top five deadliest pandemics. Modern medical advancements and
superior hygiene prevented the pandemic from being any deadlier than it was, and the pandemic was over by 2023. No
other epidemic or pandemic in the century compared to the COVID-19 pandemic in terms of mortality or societal
impact. Nonetheless, other epidemics and pandemics in the century included the worldwide <color=#3366CC>2009 swine flu pandemic</color>,
an uptick in global H1N1 influenza cases. The pandemic resulted in possibly up to 1.4 billion cases and 284,000
deaths.

• In the <color=#3366CC>National Football League</color>, the <color=#3366CC>New England Patriots</color> were the dominant franchise of the first two decades of

season. Other teams with multiple Super Bowl appearances over that time period include the Philadelphia Eagles,

quarterback <color=#3366CC>Peyton Manning</color>, who won five MVP awards, the most in history, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers who

positions include wide receiver Randy Moss, who set the record for most receiving touchdowns in a season with 23
in 2007, wide receiver Michael Thomas, who set the NFL record for most receptions in a season with 149 in 2019,
tight end Rob Gronkowski, who became the first tight end to lead the league in receiving touchdowns in 2011, and
running back Adrian Peterson, who set the all-time NFL record for rushing yards in a game with 296 in 2007, his
rookie year. Key defensive players of the century include safety Ed Reed, who led the league in interceptions three
times, linebacker <color=#3366CC>Ray Lewis</color>, who set the career tackles record when he retired in 2012, and linebacker J. J. Watt,
who is the only player to record more than 20 quarterback sacks in two different seasons.
• In American college football, the sport saw the creation of the College Football Playoff, the first playoff for NCAA
Division I Football Bowl Subdivision, the highest level of college football in the U.S. The series was dominated by
two teams, the Clemson Tigers and Alabama Crimson Tide, at least one of which has played in every Playoff since
its inception in 2014 and between them have won all but one of said championships. Prior to 2014, the method of
determining the champion was done via the Bowl Championship Series (BCS), a single championship game that
attempted to match the top two teams in the country using a series of polls and computer rankings to choose the
top two teams. In the BCS era, the top teams were Alabama, which won three BCS Championships, and Florida
State, LSU, and Oklahoma, which won two BCS Championships each. <color=#3366CC>Nick Saban</color>, who led both LSU and
Alabama to one and seven national championships respectively, was the most dominant coach of his era, while
quarterbacks dominated the Heisman Trophy, winning 16 of 20 during the first two decades of the 21st century.
Several controversies over the payment of athletes dominated the sport, with Heisman Trophy winner Reggie Bush
being forced to return his award over receiving improper benefits while maintaining amateur status, while officials
and media continued to debate the possibility of paying athletes at all levels of college athletics.

different Ottawa-based franchises failed during the first decade of the 21st century. The league found stability

Arts and entertainment
Art
The rise of the <color=#3366CC>Internet</color> and <color=#3366CC>Social Media</color> led to art being democratized and revolutionized. Art websites and spaces
such as <color=#3366CC>DeviantArt</color> grew rapidly. New art movements, such as <color=#3366CC>minimalism</color>, craftivism, stuckism, and remodernism, as
well as art forms such as <color=#3366CC>street art</color>, <color=#3366CC>environmental art</color>, and pixel art, rose as well. However, concerns grew over the
dilution and commercialization of art.
Music
At the beginning of the century, the <color=#3366CC>compact disc</color> (CD) was the standard form of music media, but alternative forms of
music media started to take its place such as music downloading and <color=#3366CC>online streaming</color>. A resurgence in sales of <color=#3366CC>vinyl</color>
<color=#3366CC>records</color> in the 2010s was driven by record collectors and audiophiles who prefer the sound of analog vinyl records to
digital recordings. In 2020, for the first time since the 1980s, vinyl surpassed CDs as the primary form of physical media
for consumers of music, though both were still surpassed by online streaming, which by the 2020s became the
predominant way that people consumed music. As of 2024, the most active music streaming services were <color=#3366CC>YouTube</color> (2
billion monthly music users, 100 million premium subscribers), <color=#3366CC>Spotify</color> (615 million monthly users, 239 million premium
subscribers), Tencent Music (576 million monthly users, 106.7 million premium subscribers), NetEase Cloud Music
(205.9 million monthly users, 44.1 million premium subscribers), Gaana (185 million monthly users), SoundCloud (175
million monthly users), JioSaavn (100 million monthly users), and Apple Music (60 million subscribers).
Television
As with music, the story of the first three decades of the 21st century was the growth of <color=#3366CC>streaming television</color> services in
competition with older forms of television, such as <color=#3366CC>Terrestrial television</color>, <color=#3366CC>cable television</color>, and <color=#3366CC>satellite television</color>. The
first major company to dominate the streaming service market was <color=#3366CC>Netflix</color>, which began as a <color=#3366CC>DVD</color>-delivery service in
the late 1990s, transitioned into an online media streaming platform initially focused on delivering content produced by
studios, then began to produce its own content, beginning with the popular and critically acclaimed series <color=#3366CC>House of</color>
<color=#3366CC>Cards</color> in 2013. Netflix's success encouraged the creation of numerous other streaming services, such as Disney+/Hulu
(Disney), YouTube Premium (Google), Amazon Prime Video, and HBO Max (WBD), the latter of which, within a year of
its launch, overtook Netflix as the most downloaded television streaming application.
Issues and concerns
• <color=#3366CC>Climate change</color>: Climate scientists have reached a consensus that the earth is undergoing significant
<color=#3366CC>anthropogenic</color>, i.e. <color=#3366CC>human</color>-induced, global warming. Global warming risks considerable <color=#3366CC>losses in biodiversity</color> and
<color=#3366CC>ecosystem services</color>, unless considerable sociopolitical changes are introduced, particularly in patterns of mass
consumption and <color=#3366CC>transportation</color>.
• <color=#3366CC>Population</color>: The world's population demographics will shift considerably, with the population of <color=#3366CC>Europe</color> and <color=#3366CC>East</color>
<color=#3366CC>Asia</color> predicted to decline considerably and the population of <color=#3366CC>Africa</color>, and to a lesser extent <color=#3366CC>South Asia</color>, to grow
considerably, unless there are policy changes. The <color=#3366CC>United Nations</color> estimates <color=#3366CC>world population</color> will reach 9.7 billion
by 2050, and peak at nearly 10.4 billion in the 2080s.
• Overconsumption and <color=#3366CC>overpopulation</color>: Such growth raises questions of ecological <color=#3366CC>sustainability</color> and creates many
<color=#3366CC>economic</color> and <color=#3366CC>political</color> disruptions. In response, many <color=#3366CC>countries</color> have adopted policies which either force or
encourage their citizens to have fewer children, and others have limited <color=#3366CC>immigration</color> or both.
• <color=#3366CC>Poverty</color>: Poverty remains the root cause of many of the world's other ills, including <color=#3366CC>famine</color>, <color=#3366CC>disease</color>, and insufficient
<color=#3366CC>education</color>. Poverty contains many self-reinforcing elements (e.g. it can make <color=#3366CC>education</color> unaffordable, which results
in continuing poverty) that <color=#3366CC>aid groups</color> hope to rectify. Progress has been made in reducing poverty, especially in
<color=#3366CC>China</color> and <color=#3366CC>India</color>, but increasingly in <color=#3366CC>Africa</color> as well.
• <color=#3366CC>War</color>: Conflicts continue around the world, such as the <color=#3366CC>Syrian Civil War</color>, the <color=#3366CC>Yemeni Civil War</color> and the
<color=#3366CC>Russo-Ukrainian War</color>. Violence continues in the <color=#3366CC>Arab–Israeli conflict</color>. Concern remains about <color=#3366CC>nuclear war</color> and
<color=#3366CC>nuclear proliferation</color> and the availability of <color=#3366CC>weapons of mass destruction</color> to rogue groups.
• <color=#3366CC>War on drugs</color>: The legal, social, and military battle by governments against drug cartels show little results in ending
drug trading and consumption, and an increase in the lives taken. After 2006 in the <color=#3366CC>Mexican drug war</color>, more than
100,000 human lives have been <color=#3366CC>lost</color>. Some <color=#3366CC>jurisdictions</color> have enacted a degree of legalization or decriminalization

of some kinds of <color=#3366CC>drugs</color> and narcotics, notably several U.S. states legalizing <color=#3366CC>marijuana</color> for <color=#3366CC>recreational</color> or <color=#3366CC>medical</color>
use.
• <color=#3366CC>Intellectual property</color>: The increasing popularity of digital formats for <color=#3366CC>entertainment media</color> such as <color=#3366CC>movies</color> and
<color=#3366CC>music</color>, and the ease of copying and distributing it via the <color=#3366CC>Internet</color> and <color=#3366CC>peer-to-peer</color> networks, has raised concerns
in the media industry about <color=#3366CC>copyright infringement (piracy)</color>. Much debate is proceeding about the proper bounds

between protection of <color=#3366CC>copyright</color>, <color=#3366CC>trademark</color> and <color=#3366CC>patent</color> rights versus <color=#3366CC>fair use</color> and the <color=#3366CC>public domain</color>, where some
argue that such laws have shifted greatly towards intellectual property owners and away from the interests of the
general public, while others say that such legal change is needed to deal with a perceived threat of new
technologies against the rights of authors and <color=#3366CC>artists</color> (or, as some put it, against the outmoded business models of
the entertainment industry).
• <color=#3366CC>Technology</color>: <color=#3366CC>Communications and control</color> technology continues to augment the intelligence of individual humans,
